_comment: Biome kits = sets of 5 textures bound to the 5 slots in terrain_blend.gdshader, plus per-kit height-band tuning. Each kit's texture IDs reference world3/textures/wgv3/<id>/.

alpine.description: High-elevation rocky terrain with snow caps. Default — matches Tetons, Cascades, Sierra.

desert.description: Arid landform: sand low, dry rock high, no snow. Mojave, mesa, dune fields.

height_bands._comment: No real snow — top band is salt-pan / sun-bleached. Push high band up so it appears only on rare plateau tops.

tundra.description: Cold low-relief terrain. Moss/lichen low, frosted rock mid, ice/snow even at moderate elevation.

height_bands._comment: Snow band lower (60% instead of 85%) — even modest elevation has frost cover at high latitudes.

temperate_forest.description: Lowland forest with bare rock peaks. Forest floor low, grass/dirt mid, rock above tree line.

height_bands._comment: Tree line (rock takes over) is around 60-70% elevation in temperate latitudes.

grassland.description: Open plains with subtle relief. Mostly grass + dirt; rock only on rare hilltops.

height_bands._comment: Loose bands by design — grassland regions (Serengeti, Tibet, Great Plains, Pantanal) are biologically near-uniform tall_grass with rare rocky outcrops. Tightening these adds fake variation that doesn't match real savanna/plateau imagery. The visual flatness in renders is faithful to the biome; visible variation comes from the macro_value_strength (Phase E topdown) not from triggering different slots. If a region needs a specific rocky landform (e.g. East African kopjes), it should be modeled in the heightmap or get its own kit, not handled by widening the height bands here.
